name: Warm Boot
tagline: The site powers on, and the signal develops into a painting.
summary: On a first visit a POST log of the company decodes to OK, collapses into one phosphor line, and a generative raster landscape rises out of it. The raster then thins scanline by scanline until only an airbrushed dawn painting is left, and the signal stays underneath for a lens to find. It presents Albretsen AS as a machine that checks itself and then gets out of the way: calm, exact and lit from below the horizon. Products are suns at their own hour, retired ones are filed as specimens.
voice: Editorial and plain, like a caption on a plate: facts first, one italic phrase of warmth per line. "Builds quiet software that pays for itself."
motion: Everything moves on a 120 ms beat: text decodes left to right, rasters open from a single line, and pictures develop as scanlines thin to nothing.
sound: Off until asked for; then a low CRT hum swells on power-on and each check lands as a soft pentatonic tick.
mark: A banded sun above a terminal-cursor bar that blinks: dawn and a prompt in one glyph, set beside the name in wide Martian Mono.
